In this regard, this paper presents a WDM-PON topology employing tunable Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Lasers (VCSELs) and a carrier reuse scheme based on Reflective Semiconductor Optical Amplifiers (RSOAs) as a 5G Analog Fronthaul configuration. Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) results are within the specifications imposed by 3GPP when operating at 3.5 GHz with 1.25 Gbps and 26 GHz with 10 Gbps.

articleTitle: Printed Strain Sensor Based on 5.5GHz Stretchable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper proposes a stretchable printed coplanar patch antenna designed for a 5.5 GHz application onto a PDMS substrate. The influence of the strain applied on the PDMS substrate using the reflection coefficient of the antenna has been investigated. The simulation has shown a 154 MHz shift of the resonant frequency for a 10% stretch. These results present a real interest for stretching sensors and mechanically tunable antenna.

articleTitle: Adaptive control for efficiency improvement in time-varying Visible Light Communication systems
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this work, we investigate and compare different techniques for dynamic adjustment of operational parameters in Visible Light Communication systems. Results show how the chosen set of control variables can drastically affect the system performance and efficiency, especially in the design of VLC systems for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference in Hospital Environment: Case Study of the Intensive Care Units of a University Hospital
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) sources are abundant in the routine of a hospital. Such sources can be for personal use, be part of the set of electromedical equipment or the building structure. This article presents the verification of electromagnetic interference between field sources and hospital devices, since electromagnetic interference is a factor that puts the correct functioning of these equipments at risk. As a consequence, patient’s lives are also put at risk. Since in many cases, the vitality of the patient depends exclusively on medical devices, electromagnetic fields were measured inside and outside the intensive care units (ICUs) of the University Hospital Alcides Carneiro (UHAC) with all hospital devices working normally. The electromagnetic field values obtained at the hospital were compared with the values imposed by the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC).

Author Keywords: electromagnetic field measurements in hospital environments

articleTitle: Matrix Conditioning Effects on Implicit Time-Domain Maxwell Solvers
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Time-domain finite-difference and finite element algorithms for Maxwell’s equations can be broadly classified as explicit or implicit. The time step increment value in explicit algorithms is often constrained by the Courant stability limit. As such, a commonly perceived advantage of implicit algorithms is their ability to employ time step increments determined solely based on accuracy criteria, as opposed to stability criteria. For problems involving highly refined grids, the Courant stability limit can be very stringent, meaning that implicit algorithms can make use of much larger time step increments than explicit algorithms. On the surface, this suggests that (proportionally) faster simulation times are possible when using implicit algorithms. However, implicit algorithms typically require a linear matrix solver at each time step. The impact of the condition number of the associated matrix is of crucial importance in assessing how the algorithm speed scales with the time step increment. In this work, we discuss the growth of the condition number with the time step increment and to what extent this growth counteracts some of the perceived advantages of implicit algorithms for Maxwell’s equations.

articleTitle: Teaching Experimental Optics for Undergraduate Students in COVID-19 Times
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work presents a viable alternative to Experimental Classes of Optics subjected to social distancing posed by COVID-19. The proposed experiments of Geometrical and Wave Optics can be conducted by the students in a home-lab basis with materials and equipment easily available. In the event of any occasional lack of these resources, an strategy was thought allowing the students to fulfill the objectives of the academic discipline.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of the heat transfer in the Z-scan experiment
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents the theoretical calculations concerns the heat transfer of the material irradiated by laser during the Z-scan experiment. The function of temperature distribution T (x, y, z, t) inside the sample was obtained by finite difference method. A new heat source model Q(x, y, z, t) suitable for thermal phenomena occurring in the Z-scan experiment was proposed. All numerical calculations simulating the discussed problem have been implemented in the ZLAMBDA program.

articleTitle: All-optical True-Time Delay for Phase Control in MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: A simple and cost effective all-optical true-time delay, based on optical frequency comb combined with fiber dispersion, is proposed. Simulation results in both the optical and RF domain show the applicability of the proposed solution in hybrid optical-radio access networks for wideband beamforming in a phased-array antenna system.

articleTitle: Simulation Software for an Optical FBG Sensor Applied in Flow Measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents a software developed in Python<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> which is applied for automating an optical Fiber Bragg Gratings (FBG) sensor calibration. By setting initial parameters and combining them with environment-captured data, the software is capable of auto-calibrating the probe, determining more precisely the FBG’s position inside the fiber. Besides that the routines may be applied for designing new probes.

articleTitle: Propagation Measurements for Indoor Environment in the 28 GHz and 38 GHz Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Mobile usage has grown exponentially in recent years, making it challenging to improve signal quality and support services requiring high data rates and low latency. The millimeter-wave frequency bands are being explored for application to the 5th Generation of Mobile Communications. From measurements performed in indoor environments, in the 28 GHz and 38 GHz frequency range, it was possible to analyze the communication channel based on the propagation models for the millimeter-wave frequency bands.

articleTitle: Spectral Analysis of a Multilayer Graphene Plasmonic Sensor operating in Far Infrared
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this paper we present a spectral analysis of a surface plasmon resonance sensor based on multilayer graphene (MLG) operating as a terahertz refractometer. This device has its structure based on the Kretschmann configuration, and the graphene layers are modeled as surface impedances with conductivity described by the Kubo model. The structure’s electromagnetic response is obtained from the multimodal model, considering TM excitation performed in a frequency range from 1 to 3Thz. In this approach we evaluate the sensor response for two, three, four and five layers of graphene, equally doped at a chemical potential of 0.45eV. As a result, we present the plasmonic response of the device, verifying the operating frequency range for each case of multilayer graphene. In addition, the sensitivity, FWHM and figure of merit are calculated to describe the sensor performance in each demonstrated case.

articleTitle: Mechanically Reconfigurable Phase Shifter for Switched-Beam Applications in mm-Waves
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a 1x8 mechanically reconfigurable phase shifter for 5G New Radio (NR) switched-beam applications. A waveguide-based 1x4 power splitter is proposed to feed four semi-circular-shaped waveguides with 8 output ports. The angular position for coupling the power splitter and the circular-shaped waveguides (γ) leads to the reconfigurable phase shifting. The proposed structure is capable to provide a phase difference between two consecutive output ports approximately fixed as Δφ for every angular coupling position and a linearly and continuously variation of Δφ from 0° to 180° by properly managing the circular-shaped waveguide.

articleTitle: High Sensitivity Envelope Detector Assisted by Microwave Photonics
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This article presents a concept of an envelope detector with a high sensitivity value based on Microwave Photonics (MWP). The process of envelope detecting of RF signals is achieved by the translation of the RF spectrum to the optical spectrum range followed by optical filtering to cut the lower sideband and the carrier. Finally beating the optical components of the remaining upper sideband into a low-speed photodetector, as a self-homodyne process. This approach depends only on the RF passing band of the phase modulator and the optical filter transfer function. This concept is experimentally demonstrated reaching envelope detector sensitivity values around 53,000 V/W for RF input frequency range of 10 GHz to 20 GHz. The proposed architecture does not use any optical or video signal amplifier. The implementation of this approach is simple, employs few components, and Commercial off-the-Shelf (COTS).

articleTitle: Hybrid ARIMA and Artificial Neural Network Modelling Applied for Electromagnetic Propagation: A Coastal City Scenario
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work shows an application of a hybrid Autoregressive Moving Average model proposed on a previous work. The scenario presented in this study is located in a city called Salinópolis in the coast of the Brazilian state of Pará. We worked in a different frequency range than that of the previous work. Now we are applying this model to the Brazilian cellular phone frequency. We worked at the range of 869 MHz to 880 MHz, which is the frequency range of one of the cell phone operators that attends the city of Salinópolis. We can see through the results of this study that the model performed its fittings feasibly in the new scenario and shows good signs of its application to a greater variety of scenarios.

articleTitle: Speed Estimation of a Three Phase Induction Motor Using Stator Dynamic Strain Measurement by Fiber Bragg Grating Sensor based in SVR
publicationTitle: 2021 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this paper, the Support Vector Regression (SVR) technique is use for speed estimation of a Three Phase Induction Motor (TIM) by the dynamic strain measurement analysis running at different load condition. The dynamic strain induced by mechanical and electrical forces is measure by fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs), installed inside the motor, in between two stator teeth. A frequency inverter driver is operating at 60 Hz to run the motor at 0%, 23.15%, 36.28%, 40.03% and 41.3% of the nominal load. The speed is estimate based on SVR with a maximum absolute error of 0.2%. The dynamic strain measured by FBGs has a good signal-to-noise ratio due to the intrinsic characteristics of optical sensors.
